role: Sr. Business Intelligence Engineer, Deal Tooling Insights, AWS GDSP Other
responsibilities: Design and build scalable data pipelines and models to derive key business metrics from large, complex datasets.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify and onboard new data sources that expand analytical coverage.
Create new metrics to measure the health of the business, support business strategy and enable the broader team to achieve its goals.
Drive the development of new data enrichment tools and self-service reporting mechanisms to help scale and optimize the reporting processes across the organization.
Conduct deep dive analyses of business problems and formulate conclusions and recommendations to be presented to senior leadership.

Communicate complex analytical results in a clear and easy-to-understand way and will drive towards simple, scalable solutions to difficult problems while considering edge cases and different tradeoffs
Build and adopt agentic capabilities that automate and accelerate analytical work, from report generation to answering analytical questions on demand.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: A keen sense of end-to-end ownership, drive, and scrappiness is a must
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Mixed: 'scrappiness', 'automate and accelerate' and 'speed to insights' sit alongside 'the highest standards', 'detail-oriented' and 'considering edge cases'.
evidence.domain_risk: The Deal Tooling and Insights team provides tools, process monitoring, and bespoke analysis to our internal customers
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Moderate: internal deal analytics that inform business decisions, with no financial reporting or regulatory language.
evidence.collaboration_width: Product Managers; Data Engineers; internal customers
evidence.data_team_maturity: You will work with datasets in one of the world's largest data warehousing environments
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Mature: an established business intelligence team inside a very large warehouse environment, with separate data engineers.
evidence.jd_authorship: Build and adopt agentic capabilities that automate and accelerate analytical work, from report generation to answering analytical questions on demand.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Mixed: the agentic-capability bullet is specific, while most bullets are generic BI duties ('Collaborate with cross-functional teams').
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Do you want to have an impact on making strategic deals come to life?
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Commercial: the audience is AWS deal-making, measured by 'adoption, engagement, and growth'.
evidence.autonomy_level: Drive the development of new data enrichment tools and self-service reporting mechanisms
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Strategic: the role drives new tooling, creates the business health metrics and helps 'shape and adopt' agentic capabilities.
evidence.ai_role: Build and adopt agentic capabilities that automate and accelerate analytical work
evidence.ai_role_explanation: AI enabler: the candidate builds agentic analytics capabilities as well as using them, and the enabler signal wins the tie.
evidence.testing_framing: No testing or data quality signal.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Absent: no testing, data quality or observability language appears.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: None: the posting is framed around insight, growth and automation, with no risk register.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Drive the development of new data enrichment tools
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Greenfield: most bullets build new pipelines, metrics, data sources, tools and agentic capabilities.
ats_keywords: information retrieval, data science, machine learning and data mining
LLMs, RAG, agent frameworks, knowledge graphs
